examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Rate λ gives survival e^(−λt), mean 1/λ and variance 1/λ² for nonnegative waiting times. Memorylessness says additional waiting conditional on survival has the original law. In a Poisson process these are interarrival times. A rate is inverse time, not a mean; convert units so λt is dimensionless. The complement of survival gives the probability of an event occurring by a deadline.

**Key relationship:** E[X]=1/λ; Var(X)=1/λ²; P(X>s+t|X>s)=e^(−λt)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify rate versus mean.
2. Use survival for beyond-time events.
3. Subtract elapsed time under memorylessness.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For waiting time X with rate λ>0, density is λe^(−λx) for x≥0 and survival P(X>t)=e^(−λt). Mean=1/λ and variance=1/λ². Its memoryless property conditions on having already waited and subtracts that elapsed time, rather than restarting the event description without conditioning.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
An exponential waiting time has mean 4 seconds. What is its variance in seconds squared?

**Answer: 16.** Mean 1/λ=4 gives λ=1/4 per second. Variance 1/λ²=16 seconds². Rate and mean are reciprocals and have different units.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The memoryless property holds for exponential continuous waiting times and geometric discrete counts, not arbitrary distributions.

The exponential rate λ is not its mean.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Exponential mean 4 minutes implies rate per minute:

- **A.** 0.5
- **B.** 0.25
- **C.** 4
- **D.** 2

**Answer: B.** λ=1/mean=1/4 per minute.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

For exponential X, choose true statements.

- **A.** E[X]=1/λ
- **B.** Var(X)=1/λ²
- **C.** P(X>s+t|X>s)=P(X>t) for s,t≥0
- **D.** Negative times have positive probability

**Answer: A, B, C.** A/B are its moments, C is memorylessness. Its support excludes negative times.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Rate is 2 per second. Find variance in s².



**Answer: 0.25.** Variance=1/λ²=1/4 s²; mean is 1/2 second.
